
6s-Block Triple-Zeta Basis Set Archive
======================================


Date: 27 Feb 2007


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, in preparation. Available from the Dirac web site, http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF orbital coefficients, given
with respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for
the basis sets described in the above articles. The SCF exponent sets reported
include the valence correlating d function. The d sets were reoptimized after
addition of the valence correlating d function, which was held fixed.  In all 
the following descriptions, this is the set referred to as the SCF exponent set. 

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of 6s6p correlating functions.

4. Exponents of 5s5p correlating functions.

5. Exponents of 4d correlating functions.

6. Exponents of 5s5p polarizing functions


Basis set construction.
----------------------

For the s elements, the outer core (n-1)s and (n-1)p must be included in the valence.
For Sr, the valence np is considered an occupied orbital and is correlated; hence 
there is an extra correlating d function for Sr. 

Several different types of basis sets may be constructed by adding primitive 
functions to the SCF set. These basis sets are described below.

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 

1. Valence and outer core. To the SCF occupied set, add the following:
   1st, 3rd, 4th, and 6th s primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 3rd, 4th, and 6th p primitives from the SCF set
   5s5p correlating 2d1f function (includes outermost 2d primitives from SCF set)
   valence correlating functions (1d for Rb, 1d1f for Sr)

   (HF + 4s4p3d1f/2f valence/outer core)


2. Core 4d correlation. To basis set 1, add the following:
   7th and 9th s primitives from the SCF set
   7th and 9th p primitives from the SCF set
   3rd and 4th d primitives from the SCF set
   3d correlating 2f1g set

   (HF + 4s4p3d1f/2f valence/outer core + 2s2p2d2f1g core)


3. Outer core (5s5p) dipole polarization. To any of the above basis sets, add the 
   s, p, d, and f polarizing functions. The p polarizing function could be omitted,
   since the p gap is fairly small. 





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================           




** Cs **
